newsitem.title: EGYPT: Ukrainian ferry runs aground on Red Sea reef.
newsitem.headline: Ukrainian ferry runs aground on Red Sea reef.

text.p: A Ukrainian ferry carrying 12 crew members but no passengers has run aground on a coral reef in the Red Sea and Egypt has sent tugs to refloat it, marine officials said on Wednesday.
The 38-metre (125-foot) Moldova struck the Woodhouse reef in the Strait of Tiran on Saturday, one official who declined to be named told Reuters.
He said it was difficult to assess at this stage whether the ferry, which was travelling from Eilat to the Black Sea, caused any damage to the reef, which is in a popular diving spot.
"The boat is okay. There is no leakage of oil," he said.
A Sharm al-Sheikh port official said early on Wednesday they were waiting for the tugboats to pull the ferry off the reef.
In April a British cruise liner ran aground in the Strait of Tiran and was detained by the Egyptian government pending payment of $23.5 million in compensation for alleged damage to the coral reef.
Egypt's tourism industry is a vital source of foreign currency and partly relies on Red Sea and Mediterranean diving.
